title: Localized encrypted-golden eval orchestrator for Dedicated & Private tenants
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated or Private deployments require regression checks tied to config/model rollouts but cannot allow golden prompts, references, or raw telemetry to leave their network. We need an eval orchestration approach that runs close to customer data, keeps reference corpora encrypted under customer-controlled keys, and produces only privacy-preserving signals to Redwood.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight 'Eval Agent' that can be deployed inside tenant VPCs or on-prem. Agent responsibilities: (1) execute scheduled and trigger-driven eval suites against candidate model/config changes, (2) store goldens encrypted with customer KMS/HSM and decrypt only locally, (3) produce hashed/aggregated regression telemetry and diffs (no raw prompts or model outputs sent outbound), and (4) integrate with Redwood Console for alerts and gated rollouts.

Constraints: minimize CPU/GPU footprint on tenant resources, avoid per-tenant heavy infra where possible, support both model binary variants and runtime config deltas, and comply with data sovereignty and audit requirements for regulated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Eval Agent can be deployed to a tenant VPC as a single container with a documented manifest
Goldens are stored encrypted with customer-managed KMS and never persist in plaintext outside tenant boundary
On model/config change trigger, agent runs defined eval suites and emits only aggregated deltas (hash-anchored) to Redwood Console
Console UI shows per-customer regression score, CI-style pass/fail gate, and recommended rollback action
Security review sign-off completed and KMS/HSM integration tested with two cloud providers
tasks: Define minimal eval suite spec and serialization format for local goldens
Design encrypted golden storage format and KMS integration pattern (customer key binds to agent)
Implement Eval Agent prototype (container) with pluggable runner for model variants
Create telemetry sanitizer that produces non-reversible hash anchors and binned statistics
Console: add tenant-scoped eval dashboard and canary rollback controls
End-to-end test with 2 pilot customers on Dedicated and 1 on Private on-prem
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Eng (runtime + infra), Security, and Solutions Engineering. Agreed target scope: regression suites + KMS integration first phase.
2026-03-04: Security asked to validate threat model for local decryption. Added ENG-21458 (KMS/HSM auth flow) to dependencies.
2026-03-06: Prototype spec drafted for agent container; initial decision to avoid sending raw model outputs—only hashed anchors + histograms allowed.

2026-03-08: Solutions Eng proposed a low-overhead runner that sends inference traffic to Dedicated GPU endpoints but executes eval logic inside agent to keep goldens local. Trade-off: slight latency and increased egress to Dedicated; logged as decision trade-off in decision_log.
2026-03-10: Security review kickoff scheduled; pilot customer outreach begun (2 interested tenants).
risks: Per-tenant compute cost: running full eval suites in-customer could be expensive—mitigation: configurable sample sizes and lightweight smoke tests
Telemetry usefulness: aggressive hashing could remove signal needed to diagnose regressions—mitigation: tiered telemetry with opt-in detailed traces under customer consent
Key management complexity: customers may use HSMs that require specialized integration—mitigation: implement pluggable KMS adapters and prioritize two cloud providers first
decision_log: Decision 2026-03-04: Keep golden corpora encrypted with customer KMS; Redwood will not hold plaintext copies for Private/Dedicated customers.
Decision 2026-03-06: Adopt hash-anchor pattern: store per-example stable non-reversible hashes to enable duplicate detection without exposing content.

Decision 2026-03-08: Use hybrid runner: agent performs goldens-based evaluations locally but can call Dedicated runtime endpoints for inference to avoid shipping large model binaries into customer infra.
Open: Evaluate a future 'shadow agent' mode that mirrors production traffic for continuous regression monitoring—needs cost/benefit analysis.
notes_for_engineering: ENG: focus first on the agent's KMS handshake and telemetry sanitizer. Provide a simple manifest that Solutions Eng can deploy into customer VPCs. Consider a 'dry-run' mode that writes artifacts to a local volume for operator inspection.
customer_communications: Draft customer-facing FAQ that explains what telemetry we collect, how goldens are protected, and the opt-in model for detailed traces. Prepare a security whitepaper for customers with compliance needs.
